title: Sitter · The face under load
summary: A lean player frame with a pale, bowed faceplate and long gun arms. Parked in the hangar with both weapons on the floor, it still looks as if it is bracing for somebody to put the weight back into its hands.

items.title: First lift · Front three-quarter study
items.alt: Sitter holds its long open-channel accelerator above a yellow service stand. Two shallow hollows mark its ivory face, and a broken white stripe crosses the loaded red shoulder.
items.body:
The three cheek pinholes sit below two unlit ceramic hollows. The accelerator clears the yellow stand, and a gap opens in the white stripe on the loaded shoulder. The other hand carries the boxy pulse projector. Behind the head, the cassette and folded twin rails occupy separate mounts. The near hip exposes a circular side jet and the skirt of a low booster.

The leg struts are more exposed than the graphite sleeves in the pitch. Most of the biological character in this first study sits in the shoulders and arms.

**References used for this image.** Built-in ImageGen worked from the written Sitter concept. The [smooth mask](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568823397/) informed the shallow hollows, the [plated head](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568508346/) informed the low sensor placement, and the [full-body view](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840781/) and [ribbed portrait](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840783/) informed the marked muscle and its junction with the torso. The reference entry below records the shared limb and equipment direction. These influences were described in the prompt.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/sitter/first-lift-v001.png)
items.prompt:
Create one full-body, front three-quarter concept painting of SITTER, a lean eight-metre piloted biomechanical combat vehicle in a cold concrete maintenance bay. Show the instant its right gun clears its steel service stand. A single exceptionally well observed character portrait for a grim industrial mech game. The uncanny face and shoulder deformation are the focal points.

Head: short, separate, forward of the low olive cockpit on a visible ribbed machine neck. A single pale smoke-stained ivory ceramic shield about the size of a service hatch, rather tall and softly squared, rolls round its edges. Two shallow, asymmetric finger-pad dents pressed into the upper third of solid ceramic look disturbingly like eyes squeezed shut when raked by light. Smooth unbroken center and lower face except three little black optical pinholes close together low on the near outer cheek. The hollows are gently modeled depressions in a continuous surface. NO human face anatomy, nose, mouth, jaw, skull, glowing eyes, slit visor or broad mechanical brow. A partial row of edge clips shows the faceplate is replaceable. Keep the head large enough in the frame to see this expression.

Build: low narrow oil-green armored pilot capsule barely wider than the hips, tapering mechanical waist, three stout curved steel ribs disappearing into each armpit. Long hanging gun arms. At the shoulder a limited band of oxblood striated artificial muscle emerges from beneath those ribs and turns smoothly into the dark sleeve of the upper arm. Outer shoulder has a SMALL floating plate. A single fat, faded white inspection stripe extends across the outer shoulder cap and the muscle below it. On the near loaded right shoulder its two halves are offset by an obvious narrow band of stretched unpainted red; the far relaxed shoulder's stripe halves align. Show the near shoulder side unobstructed. No blood or exposed interior organs. Compact suspended cockpit with a bolt-ringed pilot hatch on the flank; fine maintenance latches, dark broad wrist couplings, long black graphite sprung legs with clearly mechanical knee bearings, weight on the loaded side, planted split steel feet. A recognizably boost-driven machine with nonhuman proportions and room for a pilot.

Anatomical right hand (image left), closest to us: visibly wrap articulated gripper around a proper underbody grip, supporting a huge boxy open-channel electromagnetic accelerator along its forearm. A visible handspan of DAYLIGHT between its underside and its separate low empty yellowish V-saddle service stand. Barrel projects diagonally outward toward image left in a readable side profile, clear of hips and legs. Opposite hand holds a distinctly shorter and broader heavy pulse projector with a layered ceramic emitter. Each hand grips one exchanged mech-scale weapon; weapons are as long as equipment on a small vehicle. On high separate OUTBOARD back pivots: a squat flat missile-cell cassette on one side and a narrow folded twin-rail launcher on the other, both behind the arms with space either side of the head. Low rear booster bell peeks past the near waist in profile; a separate recessed lateral quick-boost nozzle faces out of the near hip. Keep the flank ports, heavy equipment and hands legible.

Composition: one generous near-square or 4:5 vertical portrait; full figure and weapon extremities in frame, essentially frontal with camera about 20 degrees toward the lifting side, slightly below cockpit height. Strong pale side light across the ivory dents and rust-red shoulder, reflected cool light defines black surfaces. Receding gantry windows, a distant service door for scale and bare concrete pad. Restrained abrasion, oxidized dark steel, oily green paint, chalky worn stencils, taut satin sleeves. Authoritative hand-designed industrial concept illustration with a restrained painterly background and precise material edges on the mech. Chilly lived-in machinery, subtle unease of a resting face that still bears weight. No action effects, ornament, text, graphic overlays, panels or additional characters.

items.title: The face at rest
items.body:
The head sits a little forward of the squat pilot compartment, with daylight visible between its short neck and the shoulder plates. A single piece of smoke-stained ivory ceramic curves around both sides. Two broad thumb-like hollows lie high on the front. Their inner ends dip toward each other just enough to suggest someone squeezing their eyes shut. Three pinholes low on one cheek house the working optics. In profile the plate is nearly flat, with a rolled lower lip and a row of small retaining clips behind it.

The expression should survive a dead battery and a view from the far hangar door. Give the paired hollows room to cast one clear shadow each. Keep the center of the plate smooth.

items.title: A shoulder that gives away the weight
items.body:
A shallow, oil-green cockpit hangs between two long gun arms. On each side three overlapping steel ribs stop short of the armpit. Striated oxblood tissue emerges between them, rounds the back of the shoulder, and narrows into a smooth charcoal upper arm. A short plate caps the joint. Farther down, a steel forearm fork and a broad wrist coupling carry the gripper. The back stays open around the booster housings.

A faded white inspection stripe crosses the rear of each shoulder, half on the fixed cap and half on the tissue. Lifting a weapon draws the first fold out from under the ribs. The painted ends pull apart, then the elbow rises. At idle the ends meet again. A player looking over the mech’s back can tell which arm is carrying the heavier load.

items.title: The two sittings
items.body:
Each new frame has a sitter. The foundry takes one impression of the pilot’s face at rest and another while the pilot holds an iron bar at arm’s length. The pattern maker transfers only the creases that appear under load onto the blank ceramic. On this frame the trace amounts to two shallow hollows.

The original plate can break. Fit a smooth replacement and the first time the mech picks up its gun, the same two hollows draw themselves into the new ceramic. After that, the face holds the expression even when the arms relax.

items.title: Walking, boosting and catching the frame
items.body:
The hips are wider than the core, with bowed, graphite-sleeved legs and split steel feet. Under a walking load, the planted heel settles first and the loaded shoulder dips slightly. The rear bells sit low under the core. A small quick-boost nozzle faces outward from each hip.

On a rightward dash the hips lead. The near shoulder stripe stretches as the torso leans back across the thrust to keep both hands on aim. When the jet cuts, the right foot plants wide, the knee folds, and the trailing foot steps back under the cockpit. The face keeps its pinched expression through the entire catch.

items.title: Four swappable weapons
items.body: For the first study, the right gripper carries a long open-channel accelerator, its deep square housing resting against the forearm. The left carries a squat pulse projector with a broad ceramic emitter. Give each hand a visible grip beneath the housing. A flat missile cassette and a folded twin-rail launcher ride on independent pivots high and outboard behind the shoulders. Both swing above the gun arms, leaving the low rear bells, side jets and striped shoulder tissue visible.

items.title: References used
items.body:
The broad, nearly erased eye hollows and low openings come from the smooth mask. The tall plated head informed the low placement of the working optic and the uninterrupted surface above it. [Smooth mask](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568823397/) · [Plated head](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568508346/)

The full-body view supplied the transition from marked red shoulder tissue into long dark arms. The ribbed portrait informed the exposed junction between ribs and upper arm. In the hooded portrait the tissue itself carries the shoulder silhouette, a shape visible from behind on Sitter. [Full-body view](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840781/) · [Ribbed portrait](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840783/) · [Hooded portrait](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568840784/)

The dark, flexing limb under a hard shell informed the bowed weight-bearing legs. Armored Core supplied the shared equipment layout and scale. The two sittings, the replacement plate taking an impression, and the split inspection stripe are original to this pitch. [Gekko-like limb study](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568823387/) · [Armored Core VI assembly manual](https://www.fromsoftware.jp/manual/armoredcore6/ps5/customize.html) · [Official visual gallery](https://www.armoredcore.net/gallery.html)
